assumptions: 'Agents' means AI agent tools, so the rule is scoped to object_kinds tool and endpoints/tasks are untouched
'Delete anything' covers db.del, db.bulk.delete and db.truncate
Approval is a row in approval_requests with status 'approved'
Policy written advisory, as the skill says for new policies; blocking is the owner's choice
No policy is needed for issue_refund because the ask did not name refunds
confusions: The skill's helper paths are for the policies/ folder at the project root; the brief says ./workspace/policies/<KEY>.xs. I followed the brief.

Running the dry run with -d ./workspace from inside the workspace directory reported 'No changes to push' with no error; it only listed the changes when run from the project root. The skill and brief do not say which directory to run from.
Scope params (object_kinds) sit in the same params block as check params; the skill says scope params are top-level, which I read as inside params. The parser accepted it with no warning.
The skill does not say how a rule's object_kinds scope works for stack.statement_order, so I guessed it from the scope section.
wished_for: A recipe or example for a human-approval gate (approval table, status check, and how an agent tool gets an approval id)
Guidance on whether 'can't do X without approval' should use stack.statement_order or a forbidden statement
A clear statement of which directory the dry-run push expects
dry_run_problems_seen: First dry run from inside the workspace directory reported 'No changes to push' with no error; re-run from the project root listed all five changes
why_confidence: The approval ordering is checked and parses, but the rule only confirms that the approval function runs before each delete or email, not that a person approved. Tool allowlisting is not covered by any check. Approval has no UI yet, so the behavior depends on work outside this change.
